# dsh-mcp-mgr
**One MCP registry for the whole profile** — declare an MCP server once, choose it per workspace, an
d manage every server from a panel in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar.
**English** | 简体中文
> If this plugin saves you a round of hand-editing JSON, a ⭐ star helps the next person find it.
## Why this exists
MCP servers are declared per workspace, so the same server description gets copied into every worksp
ace file that needs it — and drifts. This plugin splits the two questions that were tangled together
ce file that needs it — and drifts. This plugin splits the two questions that were tangled together:
| Question | Where it is answered now |

| *What servers exist?* | once, in a profile-scoped registry |
| *Which ones does this workspace use
?* | a `use` list in that workspace's file |
Servers move between the two files without translation, both stay hand-editable, and a workspace tha
t never adopts the plugin keeps working exactly as before: a missing `use` means its inline `mcpServ
ers` mount as they always did.
## Screenshots
*Global servers — add, edit, delete, enable or disable a server, with the profile-level `mcp-client`
registrations shown as read-only rows.*
*Workspaces — which global servers each workspace selects, plus its own local servers, dangling refe
rences and parse errors.*

ct mode mounts only the active workspace's servers.
## Features
| Surface | What it does |
| Sidebar row | sits directly under **Plugins** (`order: 1`) and opens the **MCP Servers** page in t

he centre column |
| Global servers tab | the registry: add / edit / delete / enable a server, plus

the profile-level `mcp-client` registrations as read-only rows |
| Workspaces tab | per-workspace se

lection as checkboxes, each workspace's own local servers, dangling references, parse errors |
| JSO
N editing | paste a whole `mcpServers` object or one server's JSON; the host validates it and report

s per-entry errors |
| Bulk import | import several servers at once, answering its own report |
| To
ols | servers are registered through `mcp-client`; workspace tools use the `mcp__<serverName>__<tool

>` convention |
| Panel polish | optimistic selection toggles, a 60-second background refresh, tab a
nd scroll position preserved across reloads, and a version chip carrying the installed plugin versio
scroll position preserved across reloads, and a version chip carrying the installed plugin version |
## Requirements

- Node.js `>=24.9.0`
- A DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` installation (the plugin composes into a prof

ile)
- `pnpm` 11.20.0 (`packageManager` in the root manifest pins it)
## Installation
Build both packages, pack them and hand them to the profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DeepSeek Harness afterwards; the sidebar entry appears directly under **Plugins**.
There are two packages, and both are Loader rows of their own:
| Package | Role |
| `dsh-mcp-mgr` | the host half: the registry, the sync layer, and the `mcpMgr` Typert Remote contra

ct |
| `dsh-mcp-mgr-ui` | the browser half: the sidebar row and the page it opens |
Installing the host alone leaves the sidebar row without the page it opens, so the two are built and
installed together. The packages are not on npm: the profile installs them from this repository.
`dsh plugin` (a pnpm passthrough into the profile directory) is what the script uses; the Plugins pa
ge does the same thing. The desktop profile is owned by the Electron application, so `dsh --profile
desktop` itself refuses to compose it, while `dsh plugin` still works.

## Configuration
Rules that apply to either file:

- a missing `type` is treated as Streamable HTTP; `${VAR}` expansion is supported;
- a stdio server

without `cwd` uses the workspace root;
- `serverName` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$` and is glob

ally unique — duplicates surface as conflicts;
- `"enabled": false` disables an entry without removi
ng it; absent means enabled.
The profile registry is created on the first save from the panel. Neither file has to be created by
rofile registry is created on the first save from the panel. Neither file has to be created by hand.
## Remote surface
Fourteen methods on the `mcpMgr` namespace, declared once in `src/typert.descriptors.ts` and wrapped
as the host manifest and the browser contribution, so the two faces cannot disagree about a wire na
anifest and the browser contribution, so the two faces cannot disagree about a wire name or a codec:
| Method | Purpose |

| `version` | this package's installed version, for the title chip |
| `snapshot` | the whole manage

ment view |
| `setStrictMode` · `setActiveWorkspace` | gateway state, answering the refreshed snapsh

ot |
| `apply` · `removeServer` · `setServerEnabled` | workspace-local servers |
[该节后续省略]
## Caveats
- **"Connected" means the tools are registered** (`mcp__<name>__*` present in the tool registry), no
t that the network is live. `mcp-client` exposes no live connection state, so a real disconnect cann
ot be detected without changing dsh itself. A connection that drops keeps its last tool generation a

nd reconnects with backoff.
- **The refresh button re-reads the host's last snapshot**; it does not

probe.
- The plugin polls no registry and offers no self-update: the panel shows its installed versi
on, and updating means rebuilding and reinstalling it here.
